findings.contradicts: The `Particles` module's own one-line identity, repeated verbatim in three separate rendered locations, is exactly the category-level case ('true of the whole deferred ladder') the naming-rule decision assigns to 'particle' — the module is explicitly built to generalize to inertial and oriented probes (Architecture §4.6, §7) — yet its summary sentence calls it 'tracer tracking.' Architecture §4.6 itself gets this right ('Particles are instruments… A particle is a state-carrying trajectory object: today a tracer…'), so the corpus holds both the compliant and the violating phrasing for the identical object.
findings.description: A reader meeting the Home page, the API overview, or the module docstring first (the three most prominent entry points) will conclude the module is specifically about tracers, exactly inverting the stated purpose of naming it `Particles` rather than `Tracers`. The rule was applied to the accessor renames but not re-applied to the module's own identity sentence.

findings.title: "close" spans two nested scopes (step vs. iteration) without signposting
locations: PAGE: api / Generator — "finalize! — close a step: apply the post-step forcing projections to the advanced state."
PAGE: api / Propagator — "Close an iteration: deposit the field observables…" (deposit!)
PAGE: api / Propagator — "A step! alone leaves the cache mid-iteration… the caller closes the iteration with deposit!"
findings.description: The Vocabulary page states iteration strictly contains step, but 'close' is applied to both (finalize! closes a step from inside the running step!; deposit! closes the iteration afterward) without ever saying, at either site, that the two closings are nested rather than the same event. Each individual sentence is precise; the pairing across pages is not signposted, so a reader assembling the two independently must infer the nesting from the noun alone.

findings.title: "deposit" is defined as write+mark, then split so the deposit-named verb performs only the mark
locations: PAGE: notation, §Vocabulary — "deposit | to write an observable into the cache and mark the moment it belongs to."
PAGE: api / Cache — "deposit_sample!(cache) … Record the particle velocities already written into cache … as current."
PAGE: api / Particles — "record_particle_velocities!(tracers, u) … Store the Lagrangian velocity…"
findings.description: By the glossary's own definition 'deposit' = write + mark. For the one slot where the two are separate calls, the write is performed by a plainly-named recording verb while the function carrying the 'deposit' root performs only the marking half — the inverse of what the glossary entry would lead a reader to expect from a 'deposit'-named function. The prose at each site explains the split correctly, so this is a naming residue rather than a live misunderstanding risk.

findings.title: API overview's stated page order contradicted by actual sequence
locations: PAGE: api — "SimulationRun comes first because a run is what a user builds first"
PAGE: api / Cache … api / State — actual banner order is alphabetical, SimulationRun 9th of 10
findings.contradicts: the api page's own claim about the order of "the pages below" vs. the order those pages actually appear in
findings.description: The api overview explicitly claims SimulationRun leads the page sequence for readability, but the document's own page banners run alphabetically (Cache, Forcing, GBGIsotropicTurbulence, Generator, Observables, Particles, Propagator, SimulationDomain, SimulationRun, State), placing SimulationRun ninth. May be a manuscript-assembly artifact rather than a live-site defect; worth checking the built HTML nav before treating as real.

findings.title: Three incompatible conventions for documenting a mutator's return value
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing — `set_forcing_rate!(...) -> rate`, `add_forcing_source!(...) -> N̂`, `project_forcing!(...) -> advanced_field` (arrow, no trailing sentence)
PAGE: api / Particles — `record_particle_velocities!(...) -> tracers`, `advect!(...) -> tracers` (arrow, no sentence) vs. `restart!(scheme, buffers) -> buffers` plus "Returns `buffers`." (both)
PAGE: api / Generator, Cache, Propagator — `prepare!`, `velocity_rhs!`, `step!`, `deposit!`, `fields_modified!` etc.: no arrow, trailing "Returns `x`." sentence
findings.description: The same shape of function — a `!` verb mutating and returning one argument — is documented via three different, module-specific conventions, and `restart!` alone combines two of them redundantly.

findings.title: Signature `->` arrows conflate return type with returned-argument name
locations: `uses_steady_linear_rate(forcing) -> Bool`, `history_depth(scheme) -> Int`, every `Phenomenology` function `-> Float64`/`-> Reference` (arrow = actual type)
`set_forcing_rate!(...) -> rate`, `add_forcing_source!(...) -> N̂`, `advect!(...) -> tracers`, `interpolate_at_particles!(...) -> out` (arrow = mutated argument's name, not a type)
findings.description: The identical `->` syntax means two different things depending on which module's docstrings you read: a genuine return type in some, the name of the argument handed back in others.

findings.title: Simulation's docstring splits the Reynolds-number topic across three locations
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation` — "Setting the Reynolds number / By default the run is forced and stationary…" (before `Arguments`)
same page — "- Grid mode (no `viscosity`): …" / "- Explicit mode: …" (a further bulleted block AFTER `Arguments`, before `Examples`)
findings.description: Every other type docstring in the corpus goes identity → Arguments → Examples → Fields with at most one caveat before Fields. Simulation alone interleaves a second full discursive block on the same subject after Arguments — the most structurally divergent docstring reviewed.

findings.title: Forcing's module docstring uses two catalogue lists, unlike every sibling module
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing — a 1-item list (`AbstractForcing`), then a separate bulleted list of the four hook methods, then a third bulleted list of the five strategies
PAGE: api / Cache, Generator, Observables, Particles, Propagator, SimulationDomain, SimulationRun, State, and the four Phenomenology submodules — each uses exactly one contents list
findings.description: The module-docstring template (identity → one linked contents list → optional remark) holds everywhere except Forcing, which interleaves three separate lists with prose between them.

findings.title: Two multi-keyword seeders omit # Arguments entirely
locations: PAGE: api / State — `random_solenoidal_velocity_spectral!(û, domain; kinetic_energy, envelope_wavenumber, initial_spectrum = nothing, rng = default_rng())` and `random_scalar_spectral!`, both documented in prose with no bulleted Arguments section
findings.description: Every other function/type with a comparable keyword count (VarianceController, Linear, ConstantPower, StationarityCriterion, FixedDomain, Tracers, FlowConditions, FlowParameters) uses a bulleted # Arguments list; these two keywords are no more interdependent than those siblings'.

findings.title: AdamsBashforth's citation is the only trailing "Reference:" block in the corpus
locations: PAGE: api / Particles, `AdamsBashforth` — "Reference: Adams–Bashforth applied to Lagrangian tracers as in TurTLE (Lalescu et al. 2022, …)" after the caveat admonition
contrast PAGE: api / SimulationDomain `TwoThirds`, `VarianceRescaling`, `Sreenivasan1998`, `Li2008`, `ModelSpectrum` — citations open or sit inline in the identity sentence
findings.description: No other named-method docstring in the corpus places its citation after a caveat admonition as a separately labelled trailing line; AdamsBashforth is the sole instance.

findings.title: AdamsBashforth stores a field but has no # Fields section
locations: PAGE: api / Particles, `AdamsBashforth(; order = 4)` — docstring ends after the caveat and Reference line with no # Fields
findings.description: Every other single/few-field preset type documents its field under # Fields with the "plain constructor takes the field(s) directly" sentence (Kolmogorov1941(C₂), Sreenivasan1998, PaoDissipation(α), HouLi); AdamsBashforth skips it despite order plainly being a stored field.

findings.title: Named-tuple return shape stated two different ways
locations: PAGE: api / Observables, `energy_spectrum` — dedicated closing sentence "Returns a named tuple `(; wavenumbers, energy)`"
PAGE: api / Generator, `velocity_integrating_factor` — named-tuple fields (coefficient, offset_scale, offset) stated only mid-paragraph, no analogous trailing sentence
findings.description: Both return a named tuple whose shape the corpus's own rule says must be stated explicitly, but the two do it in different forms and positions.

findings.title: ModelSpectrum's Fields sentence duplicates its own top signature verbatim
locations: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra, `ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation)` shown as the sole top signature; # Fields opens "The plain constructor `ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation)` takes the three fields directly"
findings.description: Elsewhere the Fields "plain constructor" sentence demotes an alternate positional form distinct from a keyword form shown at top (e.g. HouLi); here there is no keyword form to demote from, so the sentence restates rather than adds information.

findings.title: VarianceRescaling's `over` keyword is explained twice at different granularities
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceRescaling` — full bulleted `:band`/`:total` breakdown in prose before Arguments, then a terse restatement inside Arguments
findings.description: No sibling forcing double-documents one of its keywords this way; comparable enumerable settings elsewhere are explained exactly once, inside Arguments.

findings.title: Arguments sections open with an inconsistent blanket qualifier
locations: PAGE: api / Generator, `FlowConditions` and PAGE: api / SimulationDomain, `FixedDomain` — "Arguments / All keyword, all required:"
PAGE: api / Forcing, `Linear`/`ConstantPower`/`VarianceRescaling`/`VarianceController` and PAGE: api / Particles, `Tracers` — "Arguments" with no lead-in sentence
findings.description: Roughly half the multi-keyword types state a blanket qualifier before the bullets, half do not; minor but consistent enough to normalize.

findings.title: A few caveats read as continuous prose rather than a titled aside
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationDomain, `FixedDomain` — "Nothing here defaults: …" placed like a caveat before # Fields but without the short-title-then-body shape most caveats elsewhere show
findings.description: Possibly an extraction artifact of how this manuscript glues an admonition's title onto its body; worth checking the built HTML to see whether this paragraph is actually a titled !!! note.

findings.title: The glyph G denotes two unrelated dimensionless constants, undisclosed
locations: src/Forcing.jl:531 — "the dimensionless gain ``G``" (VarianceController's feedback gain)
src/phenomenology/Scalings.jl:14 — "the box-normalized dissipation group ``G``" (Li2008's G ≈ 0.9)
src/SimulationRun.jl:190 — "``G \approx 0.9`` a dimensionless constant"
findings.contradicts: src/Propagator.jl:240-241 and :245-246 explicitly disambiguate the near-identical clashes A vs A_i and Williamson's N vs the grid N ('unrelated to the forcing rate A(κ)'; 'not the grid points N of the rest of the documentation') — the corpus discloses symbol reuse elsewhere but not for G
findings.description: VarianceController's feedback gain and Li2008's box-normalized dissipation group are unrelated physical quantities sharing the bare glyph G across two modules' public docstrings, with no cross-reference either way and no entry in docs/src/notation.md for either sense — inconsistent with the corpus's own demonstrated practice of flagging exactly this kind of clash (A/A_i, N/N).

findings.title: Three house-reserved glyphs (ε, L, T) reused, undisclosed, in one admonition
locations: src/Particles.jl:321-325 — "for a perturbation ``\epsilon`` and Lipschitz constant ``L``, Grönwall bounds the trajectory error by ``\epsilon(\mathrm{e}^{LT} - 1)/L``"
findings.contradicts: docs/src/notation.md:98 reserves L for the periodic-box side length (side_length); docs/src/notation.md:106 reserves T for the real element type (element_type); the corpus otherwise reserves \varepsilon for the dissipation rate — all three glyphs are reused bare here for an unrelated generic Grönwall bound with no disambiguating remark
findings.description: L and T are reused verbatim for a Lipschitz constant and a time span in a self-contained AdamsBashforth admonition, colliding with the same bare glyphs the rest of the package binds to box side length and element type; \epsilon (rather than \varepsilon) at least avoids literally colliding with the dissipation rate, but the other two are unremarked reuses in a corpus that elsewhere discloses this kind of clash (see the G finding's contrast with Propagator.jl's A/A_i and N/N call-outs).

findings.title: \mathrm d bracing drifts across the corpus for the identical differential
locations: src/Forcing.jl:197 — ``\int A\,\mathrm dt`` (unbraced)
src/phenomenology/Spectra.jl:104 — ``\int_0^\infty E(\kappa)\,\mathrm d\kappa = k`` (unbraced)
src/Observables.jl:301 and src/Phenomenology.jl:216 — the identical formula ``k = \int_0^\infty E(\kappa)\,\mathrm{d}\kappa`` (braced)
findings.contradicts: The house TeX-idiom rule calls for braced group arguments throughout (CLAUDE.md: 'braced group arguments … never \tfrac12 / \boldsymbol u'); the identical formula k = ∫E(κ) dκ appears word-for-word both braced (Phenomenology.jl:216, Observables.jl:301) and unbraced (Spectra.jl:104) elsewhere in the same corpus
findings.description: Three sites spell the differential as \mathrm dt / \mathrm d\kappa (no braces around the d), while six sites spell the same differential as \mathrm{d}t / \mathrm{d}\kappa. Both render identically since \mathrm binds only the next token either way, which is why the drift went unnoticed, but it is a genuine source-level inconsistency in an idiom the house style otherwise insists on bracing.

findings.title: Delimiter sizing for the Lamb-vector gradient term is not applied by one rule
locations: src/Generator.jl:417 (display math) — ``\nabla\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}\lvert\boldsymbol{u}\rvert^{2}\bigr)`` (sized)
src/Generator.jl:421 (inline math, six lines later) — "the ``\nabla(\tfrac{1}{2}\lvert\boldsymbol{u}\rvert^{2})`` gradient" (plain parens)
src/phenomenology/Spectra.jl:129 (inline math) — ``f_L(\kappa \ell) = \Bigl(\frac{\kappa \ell}{\sqrt{(\kappa \ell)^2 + c_L}}\Bigr)^{5/3 + p_0}`` (sized, inline)
findings.contradicts: If the intent were 'display math gets \bigl/\bigr, inline math gets plain parentheses', Spectra.jl:129/177/373 contradict it by using \Bigl(…\Bigr) for a comparable fraction-in-parens construct while inline; the identical Lamb-vector fragment gets both treatments six lines apart in the same file (Generator.jl:417 vs :421)
findings.description: Low confidence because the two fraction shapes differ (bare \tfrac{1}{2} vs. a \frac{}{} with a \sqrt{} in the denominator) and could independently justify different sizing by glyph height rather than by an inline/display rule. Flagged because the identical formula is sized in one rendering and bare in another within the same file, showing the choice was not applied by a conscious rule at the point of authorship.

findings.title: Architecture.md claims only EndpointHeun exists today; API ships a second scheme, AdamsBashforth
locations: PAGE: architecture, §4.6: "today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
PAGE: api / Particles: "Two members today: `EndpointHeun` … and `AdamsBashforth`, a multistep method that buys more…"

findings.title: Home page and API-overview one-liners for Particles are stale (only mention second-order Heun)

PAGE: api (overview): "Particles: Lagrangian tracer tracking — `Tracers`, second-order `advect!` (Heun-in-time), and `interpolate_at_particles!`…"

findings.title: Architecture's blanket 'every forcing has both constructor forms' overstates VarianceController/NoForcing

findings.title: restart! carries both a -> buffers arrow and a redundant "Returns buffers." sentence

findings.title: VarianceController's "marginal law" written A = ε/2k, contradicting its own formula's 2k_f
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing — VarianceController: "The rate is the marginal law $A = \varepsilon/2k$ plus a proportional restoring term"
PAGE: api / Forcing — the display immediately below: "$\frac{\varepsilon(t) - G[k(t)-k_\infty]/t_\ell}{2k_f(t)}$"
PAGE: decisions — §References, Bassenne entry: "the marginal law $A = \varepsilon/2k$ plus a proportional restoring term"
PAGE: decisions — decision 58: "Its marginal term $\varepsilon/2k_f$ reinjects exactly what dissipation removes"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: decisions, decision 58 — "Its marginal term $\varepsilon/2k_f$" — axis: which variance normalizes the rate, whole-field k or forced-band k_f
findings.description: Only ε/(2k_f) reinjects ε: the forcing acts in the band, so its injected power is 2A·k_f. With 2k the power becomes ε·k_f/k ≠ ε. The Forcing docstring contradicts itself across adjacent blocks — its next paragraph says "The two variances there are not interchangeable" — and the References blurb repeats the slip. Decision 58's own postscript records this exact k-for-k_f substitution as the near-shipped physics bug.
findings.resolution_hint: Write A = ε/(2k_f) in both prose sites.

findings.title: Two glyphs for one length: L₁₁ vs ℓ₁₁, inside the glossary itself
locations: PAGE: notation — Derived scales: "$\ell$ | the length a large-scale roll-off is evaluated against ($\ell_{11}$, or Pope's $\ell_0 = k^{3/2}/\varepsilon$)"
PAGE: notation — adjacent row: "$L_{11}$ | longitudinal (parallel) integral length scale"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra — large_scale_length: "The default is the longitudinal integral scale $L_{11}$" … "related by $\ell_{11}/\ell_{0} = C_\varepsilon (2/3)^{3/2}$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation, adjacent row — "$L_{11}$ | longitudinal (parallel) integral length scale" — axis: the glyph naming the measured longitudinal integral scale
findings.description: The glossary binds the integral scale to L₁₁ and, one row above, calls it ℓ₁₁. large_scale_length uses both in one paragraph. A reader must guess whether ℓ₁₁ is a third length beside L₁₁ and ℓ₀. The relation ℓ₁₁/ℓ₀ = C_ε(2/3)^{3/2} itself checks out; only the symbol drifts.
findings.resolution_hint: Pick L₁₁ everywhere (it is what the glossary and integral_scale use).

findings.title: L reused for the roll-off length, against its glossary binding as the box side
locations: PAGE: notation — Numerics: "$L$ | box side ($\Omega = [0,L)^3$)"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra — large_scale_length: "($\int E\,\mathrm d\kappa \propto L^{2/3}$)"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra — ModelSpectrum: "reads $\varepsilon$ and the roll-off's own length $L$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation, Numerics — "$L$ | box side" — axis: which length the symbol L denotes
findings.description: LargeScaleFactor gets this right ("$\ell$ … not the box side $L$"), but ModelSpectrum and large_scale_length then call the roll-off length L. The claim ∫E dκ ∝ L^{2/3} is true of ℓ and false of the box side, so the reuse turns a correct scaling into a wrong-looking one.
findings.resolution_hint: Use ℓ in both places, as ModelSpectrum's own display formula f_L(κℓ) already does.

findings.title: "Four strategies are provided" — then five are listed in the same sentence
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.4: "Four strategies are provided. `NoForcing` (free decay) and `Linear` … `ConstantPower` … `VarianceController` … `VarianceRescaling`"
PAGE: api / Forcing — module map lists NoForcing, Linear, ConstantPower, VarianceController, VarianceRescaling
PAGE: Home: "the forcing menu `NoForcing`, `Linear`, `ConstantPower`, `VarianceController` (the default), and `VarianceRescaling`"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Forcing and PAGE: Home — both enumerate five strategies — axis: the count of provided forcings
findings.description: A plain count error. The same paragraph later says "these four methods are written through tensor-order-generic field operators", which compounds it: five implementations share that property.
findings.resolution_hint: "Five strategies are provided", or exclude NoForcing explicitly.

findings.title: "Eddy-turnover time" carries two values differing by a factor 3/2
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing — VarianceController: "the large-eddy turnover time $t_\ell$. When omitted it is taken as $2k_\infty/3\varepsilon_\infty$"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun — StationarityCriterion: "normalizes the eddy-turnover clock $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$"
PAGE: architecture §4.7: "to normalize the eddy-turnover clock $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / SimulationRun — "the eddy-turnover clock $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$" (turnover = k/ε) — axis: the numerical definition of one named timescale
findings.description: Both definitions are defensible (u'²/ε and k/ε), but the docs name them identically and never say they differ. A user setting min_turnovers/window_turnovers against the controller's settling time t_ℓ/G is comparing units that differ by 3/2.
findings.resolution_hint: State the definition at each site, or note the 2/3 relation once.

findings.title: The IFRK2-vs-RK3 register count does not decompose as the architecture claims
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.5: "three spectral registers per field against the low-storage scheme's two, counting the same way on both sides: the scheme's own registers plus the dealiasing seam's assembly register"
PAGE: architecture §9: "an `IFLowStorageRK3` run carries neither of the two registers `IFRK2` adds"
PAGE: api / Propagator — IntegratorBuffers: "`nonlinear` — the assembled right-hand side; `IFLowStorageRK3` only"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Propagator, IntegratorBuffers — "`nonlinear` … `IFLowStorageRK3` only" — axis: which registers each scheme carries, and whether RK2's set contains RK3's
findings.description: By the field lists RK2 = {stage1, stage2, velocity_predictor_spectral} and RK3 = {stage1, nonlinear}: RK2 gains two and loses one, so "the two registers IFRK2 adds" over-counts and 3-vs-2 cannot follow from it. The "own registers + one assembly register" decomposition also fails for RK2, which carries no assembly register — its third slot is the predictor.
findings.resolution_hint: State the two sets and their difference rather than an "adds" relation.

findings.title: E_φ(κ) is a density but is glossed with a sum
locations: PAGE: notation — Diagnostics: "$E_\varphi(\kappa)$ | the scalar-variance spectrum, summing to $\langle\varphi^{2}\rangle$"
PAGE: notation — adjacent rows: "$E(\kappa)$ … $k = \int_0^\infty E(\kappa)\,\mathrm{d}\kappa$" and "$E_n$ … $k = \sum_n E_n$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation, adjacent rows — the density E(κ) integrates while the per-shell E_n sums — axis: density vs per-shell quantity
findings.description: Spectra.ObukhovCorrsin1949 defines E_φ(κ) as a per-unit-wavenumber density (dimensions [φ²]·L, checked), and random_scalar_spectral! takes it as "a target radial scalar-variance spectrum". "Summing" makes a reader carry the wrong Δκ factor — the E_n/E(κ) confusion decision 24 exists to prevent. The row also omits dimensions where both neighbours give them.
findings.resolution_hint: "integrating to ⟨φ²⟩", and add the dimensions.

findings.title: ObservablesCache's rendered signature omits history_depth, which its Arguments list documents
locations: PAGE: api / Cache: "`ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)`"
PAGE: api / Cache — Arguments: "`history_depth = 1` — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over, including the current one"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Cache — the signature block above the same docstring — axis: the keyword set of one constructor
findings.description: A reader copying the signature cannot build a cache for AdamsBashforth, whose MultistepBuffers reads the sample history from the cache. The keyword is documented and consumed but invisible where a user first reads it.
findings.resolution_hint: Add history_depth = 1 to the signature line.

findings.title: allocate_buffers' documented signatures miss the three-argument multistep form
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator — allocate_buffers: "`allocate_buffers(scheme, domain; scalar = false)`" / "`allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers)`"
PAGE: api / Particles — MultistepBuffers: "Build it with `allocate_buffers``(scheme, tracers, cache)`"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Particles, MultistepBuffers — "allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers, cache)" — axis: the generic's documented method set
findings.description: The generic's docstring is the home for its methods and says "The second serves the trajectory schemes" as if EndpointHeun's form were the only one. The AdamsBashforth allocation call appears nowhere on the page that owns the verb.

findings.title: The Particles module map names only a subset of the module's documented surface
locations: PAGE: api / Particles — module map: Tracers, particle_positions, number_of_particles, AbstractParticleIntegrator, EndpointHeun, ParticleIntegratorBuffers, record_particle_velocities!, advect!, interpolate_at_particles!
PAGE: api / Particles — the page then documents AdamsBashforth, MultistepBuffers, restart!, history_depth
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Particles — the same page's own docstring sections — axis: map completeness
findings.description: Four documented operations are absent from the map that claims to list the module's contents; restart! in particular is one a hand-run loop must call after repositioning tracers. A map naming a subset is stale even when literally true.
