findings.title: The "resolution bound" on Δt is a lowest-mode diffusive-decay cap
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun — Simulation, max_dt: "a resolution bound $1/(D\kappa_{\min}^{2})$ built from the run's own diffusivity and box"
findings.description: Dimensionally sound (Dκ² is a rate) and κ_min is the right choice for the stated purpose — stopping the integrating factor annihilating every mode. But "resolution bound" names the opposite intuition: every other resolution statement on the site is about κ_max (κ_max η, max_wavenumber), so a reader will read this as a small-scale criterion built from the wrong wavenumber.
findings.resolution_hint: Name it for what it bounds, e.g. "a lowest-mode diffusive-decay bound".

findings.title: The CatmullRom floors quoted at 64³ and 128³ do not follow the stated Δx^{d+1} scaling
locations: PAGE: api / Particles — EndpointHeun: "a degree-$d$ interpolant's trajectory floor falls as $\Delta x^{d+1}$" … "at $N = 128$, floor $1\times10^{-5}$"
PAGE: decisions — decision 57: "`CatmullRom` ($C^1$, degree 2) floors at $1.2\times10^{-5}$" (measured at $64^3$)
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Particles, EndpointHeun — "floor falls as $\Delta x^{d+1}$" — axis: the measured floor's resolution scaling
findings.description: Degree 2 implies a Δx³ floor, so doubling N should drop it roughly eightfold; the two quoted numbers agree to within 20 %. The measurements are on different fields (frozen ABC vs "a band-limited field"), which may account for it, but neither page says so, and the two numbers sit one page apart under a single scaling claim.
findings.resolution_hint: Name the test field beside each number, or quote both floors from one study.

findings.title: Same DOI, two different paper titles for the Lalescu et al. (2022) citation
locations: api / Particles, AdamsBashforth docstring: "Lalescu et al. 2022, TurTLE: a fast and scalable code for turbulence, Comput. Phys. Commun. 278, 108406, doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2022.108406"

architecture, §References: "Lalescu, C. C., Bramas, B., Rampp, M. & Wilczek, M. (2022). An efficient particle tracking algorithm for large-scale parallel pseudo-spectral simulations of turbulence. Comput. Phys. Commun. 278, 108406."
findings.contradicts: Same journal/volume/page/DOI (10.1016/j.cpc.2022.108406) cited under two different titles — 'TurTLE: a fast and scalable code for turbulence' vs 'An efficient particle tracking algorithm for large-scale parallel pseudo-spectral simulations of turbulence'.
findings.description: CLAUDE.md requires the inline docstring copy of a reference to be verbatim-consistent with its §References entry. This DOI appears with two different titles in two places, so one of them misnames the paper — a reader following either citation to check the bibliography finds an apparent mismatch.

findings.title: Named methods (Nosé–Hoover; 'Kaneda's' result) invoked with no citation
locations: api / Forcing, VarianceController docstring: "is the Nosé–Hoover move. A gain-limited relaxation ... is Berendsen weak coupling (Berendsen et al. 1984, doi:10.1063/1.448118)"
api / phenomenology / Spectra, ExponentialDissipation docstring: "consistently predict (Sagaut & Cambon 2018 ...; the closure result is originally Kaneda's)"
findings.description: In both cases a named eponymous method sits beside another named method in the same sentence that does carry a full author-year/DOI citation (Berendsen 1984; Sagaut & Cambon 2018), while Nosé–Hoover and 'Kaneda's' result get no year, reference, or §References entry anywhere in the manuscript — inconsistent citation hygiene for named/published methods.

findings.title: Obukhov's (1962) co-discovery of Kolmogorov1962 cited inline but absent from the page's References list
locations: api / phenomenology / StructureFunctions, Kolmogorov1962 docstring: "proposed independently by Obukhov (1962, J. Fluid Mech. 13, 77) in the same issue"
api / phenomenology / StructureFunctions, §References: lists Kolmogorov (1941), Kolmogorov (1962), She & Lévêque (1994), Yaglom (1949), Lundgren (2002) — no Obukhov entry
findings.description: Every other multi-author law on this page (She–Lévêque, Yaglom) gets its own full References entry, but Obukhov's independently-published co-attribution for the Kolmogorov1962 law itself — given inline with a full journal/volume/page — does not, unlike incidental-coefficient citations the page explicitly exempts (e.g. Sagaut & Cambon). Possibly covered by that exemption, possibly a genuine gap since it names a co-author of the law itself; flagged at low confidence.

findings.title: Subject-verb disagreement: "Bassenne report O(1-10)"
locations: api/Forcing, VarianceController Arguments: "Larger relaxes faster; Bassenne report $O(1-10)$." (verified in docs/build/api/Forcing/index.html, not an extraction artifact)
findings.description: "Bassenne" (a singular proper noun/citation) is paired with the plural verb "report" with no expressed plural subject — contrast the same page's correctly formed "Bassenne, Urzay, Park & Moin (2016, Eq. 20)" and elsewhere "Sreenivasan (1995) found" (singular verb with singular author). Reads as a dropped "et al." or a missing final "s" ("Bassenne reports"). This is the one clear violation of the corpus's own grammatical-prose rule found on a close pass.
findings.resolution_hint: Change to "Bassenne et al. report" or "Bassenne reports".

findings.title: Three different "no DOI" formats inside Phenomenology's own reference lists
locations: StructureFunctions References: "...30, 301–305 (the 2/3 law) and 32, 16–18 (the exact 4/5 law); no DOI, the 1941 Doklady notes predate the system" — bare trailing clause, no parens at all
StructureFunctions References, next entry: "Yaglom (1949), Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 69, 743 (no DOI: a 1949 Doklady note)" — explained parenthetical
Spectra References: "Obukhov (1949), Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR, Ser. Geogr. Geofiz. 13, 58 (no DOI) / Corrsin (1951)..." — bare two-word parenthetical, no explanation
findings.contradicts: The already-adjudicated finding covers only a capitalization difference between ARCHITECTURE.md and Phenomenology ('No DOI' vs 'no DOI'); this is a different, unaddressed axis — three distinct structural forms for the identical fact, all three inside Phenomenology's own two reference lists.
findings.description: The same fact (citation predates the DOI system) is expressed as an unparenthesized trailing clause, an explained parenthetical, and a bare unexplained parenthetical, all within the self-contained Phenomenology leaf's own bibliography lists, which are supposed to be internally uniform.

findings.title: Phenomenology's page-level References sections use the labelled DOI link form, not the bare-autolink form assigned to a References surface
locations: decisions page (carries ARCHITECTURE's Sec-References): renders as bare autolink, link text = the URL itself, e.g. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022112056000317
api/phenomenology/Scalings (and Spectra, StructureFunctions) '## References' sections: render with the labelled form instead, e.g. doi:10.1063/1.869575
findings.contradicts: CLAUDE.md states 'a Sec-References entry ends in a bare autolink ... an inline docstring cite uses the labelled [doi:10....]' — one form per surface. Both the decisions page's References and each Phenomenology submodule's own '## References' section are page-level bibliography lists (the same kind of surface), yet use the two different forms.
findings.description: Plausibly by design (a Reference value is rendered once and reused for both the inline citation and the page-level roundup, so it can only carry one format, whereas ARCHITECTURE.md's entries are hand-authored twice) but the stated rule as written does not carve out this case, and the visual inconsistency is real in the rendered site.
findings.resolution_hint: Either state the carve-out once in CLAUDE.md's rule, or render Phenomenology's References list with the bare-autolink form to match the other surface.

findings.title: The Lagrangian sample carries four near-synonymous names, and the module docstring documents the multiplicity instead of picking one
locations: api/Particles module docstring: 'the trajectory velocities are read from the run's observables cache through particle_velocities — the same quantity the docs also call the Lagrangian velocity or the trajectory velocity'
Cache glossary 'deposit' entry: 'the trajectory sample'
ObservablesCache / particle_velocities docstrings: 'the genuine Lagrangian velocity'
findings.description: Five different phrasings appear for one measured quantity u(t_n, X(t_n)): particle_velocities (the code name, used consistently), trajectory velocity, Lagrangian velocity, trajectory sample, and 'the sample'. The Particles module docstring flags the multiplicity ('the docs also call') rather than converging on one prose term. notation.md's Vocabulary section fixes one term for iteration/deposit/slot/epoch/register/front door/observation/chart/resolved but has no entry disambiguating this concept, despite it being exactly the kind of multiply-named object that section exists to pin down.

findings.title: Elliptical "Larger relaxes faster" compounds the awkwardness of the adjacent grammar slip
locations: api/Forcing, VarianceController Arguments: 'Larger relaxes faster; Bassenne report O(1-10).'
findings.description: The elided-subject construction ('a larger gain' -> 'Larger') matches an established house idiom used correctly elsewhere (e.g. kappa_max_eta's 'higher trades Reynolds number for margin'), so on its own it is not a defect. Flagged only because it sits in the same sentence as the Bassenne subject-verb error, compounding that bullet's awkwardness; low confidence this needs independent action beyond fixing the grammar error.

findings.title: ConstantPower's band-kernel storage contradicts itself across pages
locations: PAGE api / Forcing, ConstantPower Fields: "band — the band-pass kernel, lazy: ... so no indicator array is stored."
PAGE decisions, 2026-08 entry: "Linear and ConstantPower keep one materialized real indicator each for the rate fill."
findings.contradicts: PAGE decisions (2026-08 frame-compression entry) says ConstantPower keeps a materialized indicator array; PAGE api/Forcing's own ConstantPower docstring says its band kernel is lazy and no indicator array is stored — opposite claims about the same object's residency.
findings.description: A reader takes ConstantPower's own docstring at face value (lazy, nothing stored), then the decision log's supposedly-final word on frame compression asserts the opposite for the same type. One of the two is wrong about the current code, and there is no way for a first-time reader to know which.

findings.title: Particles module map omits AdamsBashforth, contradicted on the same page
locations: PAGE api / Particles, module map: "AbstractParticleIntegrator, EndpointHeun — the trajectory time-integration schemes."
PAGE api / Particles, later on the same page: "Two members today: EndpointHeun ... and AdamsBashforth."
findings.contradicts: Same page: the module map names EndpointHeun as if it were the only concrete trajectory scheme (definite article, exhaustive reading), while the page's own AbstractParticleIntegrator docstring lists AdamsBashforth as a second member.
findings.description: A reader who stops at the module map — precisely the map's job — walks away thinking EndpointHeun is the only trajectory scheme and would never look for AdamsBashforth or MultistepBuffers. The same omission repeats on the Home and api-overview pages' Particles bullets, so it is not a one-off slip.

findings.title: "epoch" used unglossed on the very first page of the site
locations: PAGE Home, Quick start comment: "each recorded against the epoch of the state it came from."
PAGE notation, Vocabulary: "epoch | a counter of changes to the state..." (first actual definition)
findings.description: "Epoch" is package-specific and load-bearing for the whole cache/staleness story, yet it first appears with zero gloss in the very first code example a newcomer reads. The Notation page's Vocabulary entry that defines it does not arrive until three pages later, and the full Cache explanation not until six pages later.

findings.title: The Decision log page precedes the glossary that defines its own vocabulary
locations: PAGE decisions (page 3): "epoch-dated, memoized charts," "the armed-rate pin," "a slot doubles as its producer's register" — all unglossed here.
PAGE notation (page 4), Vocabulary section: where epoch/chart/register/slot/deposit/iteration are actually defined.
findings.description: Read top-to-bottom as instructed, a newcomer hits the dense decision log — full of chart, epoch, register, armed, holder, reified — a full page before the one glossary that defines any of them. Audit-register jargon (holder, FIX, PF-RAISE, ledger, floor) is never defined anywhere on the user-facing site at all, glossary included.

findings.title: Top-level Observables summaries omit max_speed
locations: PAGE Home, Observables bullet lists diagnostics, skewness, spectrum scales, vorticity recovery — no max_speed.
PAGE api, Observables bullet: identical omission.
PAGE api / Observables (module's own page) lists max_speed explicitly.
findings.description: Both top-level summaries of Observables describe it as having four kinds of content and silently drop max_speed, which is present and explained at length on the module's own page. A reader who only skims the summaries would not know the CFL-setting reduction lives in this module at all.

findings.title: "advance" is overloaded across at least four distinct referents
locations: PAGE api / SimulationRun: advance!(sim), the per-iteration driver.
PAGE notation, Vocabulary "deposit" entry: "the tracer advance writes" — unglossed here.
PAGE api / Cache, particles_modified!: "tracer advance (advect! followed by record_particle_velocities!, both inside advance!)" — glossed only here, pages later.
PAGE api / Particles: "advance! pushes it every iteration."
findings.description: A cold reader meets "the tracer advance" in the Notation glossary itself with no indication it names a two-function bundle, distinct from both the top-level advance!(sim) and the specific advect! verb; "push" then floats in as a fourth informal synonym. The clarifying parenthetical exists only pages later, on the Cache page.

findings.title: current_step used at the Cache page before its own definition
locations: PAGE api / Cache, ObservablesCache docstring: "the clock's current_step answers 'how far has the run gone?'"
PAGE api / SimulationRun, Clock accessors: "current_step(sim) — The number of steps sim has taken." (first actual documentation)
findings.description: The Cache page leans on current_step to explain the epoch/clock distinction before the reader has seen current_step documented anywhere. The name is self-explanatory enough not to derail a reader, but it is still a forward reference in a corpus that is otherwise careful to gloss inline.

findings.title: StationarityCriterion's listed field name doesn't match its own keyword
locations: PAGE api / SimulationRun, StationarityCriterion: constructor keyword gate_skewness, but Fields section reads "gate_skew, min_turnovers, window_turnovers, tol and skew_floor all live inside monitor."
findings.description: The docstring already flags that fields aren't the keywords, so this may be deliberate — but the internal field is named gate_skew, one syllable short of the keyword gate_skewness, which reads exactly like the near-miss typo class the rest of the corpus is scrupulous about avoiding. Worth confirming it isn't a stale field name.

findings.title: api overview's claimed reading order doesn't match the page order it sits in
locations: PAGE api: "SimulationRun comes first because a run is what a user builds first."
Actual sequence: Cache, Forcing, GBGIsotropicTurbulence, Generator, Observables, Particles, Propagator, SimulationDomain, SimulationRun, State — SimulationRun ninth of ten.
findings.description: Taken at face value this is a real ordering mismatch a first-time reader would notice immediately. Flagged at low confidence because a near-identical ordering complaint in an earlier round turned out to be a manuscript-extraction artifact (alphabetical file dump) rather than a defect in the built site.

findings.title: "band" used repeatedly before any definition of the concept
locations: PAGE api / Forcing, module map: "Linear — a fixed linear rate on a band." (first use, undefined)
findings.description: Inferable from the lowest_shell/highest_shell keywords a few lines later and the earlier "shell" glossary entry, so severity is low — but "band" itself (a contiguous range of shells) never gets its own stated definition, unlike "shell," which has a Notation entry.

findings.title: `particles_modified!` says the run's own tracer advance both is and is not announced
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, `particles_modified!`: "The run's own tracer advance is not such a change and keeps its history."
PAGE: api / Cache, same docstring, next paragraph: "the run layer announces its own tracer advance (`advect!` followed by `record_particle_velocities!`, both inside `advance!`)"
findings.contradicts: Same docstring, three sentences apart — axis: whether `advance!`'s own tracer push is an announced (history-discarding) reposition.
findings.description: PARAPHRASE fails: the two sentences cannot both be restated truly. Either the run layer calls this verb on every push — and then the history it discards is the history a multistep scheme needs — or it does not, and the "sanctioned mutator" sentence names the wrong call. A reader wiring a hand-run loop cannot tell which.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: say once who calls it, and name what `advance!` actually does instead.

findings.title: "Four strategies are provided" — five are then named
locations: PAGE: architecture, §4.4: "Four strategies are provided. `NoForcing` (free decay) and `Linear` …" then also names `ConstantPower`, `VarianceController`, `VarianceRescaling`
PAGE: api / Forcing, module map lists all five under "The strategies"
findings.contradicts: The sentence's own enumeration — axis: how many forcing strategies ship.
findings.description: The count and the list disagree inside one paragraph. `VarianceController` was added later and the numeral was never re-counted, so the sentence reads as a stale headline over its own content.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: drop the numeral, or make it five.

findings.title: The glossary defines "resolved" as reification; the architecture defines it as resolved-versus-filtered
locations: PAGE: notation, Vocabulary: "resolved | in ResolvedFields and ResolvedGenerator, made concrete as one value."
PAGE: decisions: "`ResolvedFields` ↔ `ResolvedGenerator`, resolved against filtered, with `FilteredGenerator` … the eventual LES sibling"
findings.contradicts: The glossary entry — axis: which sense of "resolved" the type names carry.
findings.description: The glossary is the page a reader consults for exactly this word and gives the wrong sense: "made concrete as one value" is *reified*, whereas the names encode the Mori–Zwanzig resolved/filtered axis. The entry then warns about a third (numerical) reading, so the reader leaves with two senses, neither the intended one.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE the glossary entry to the resolved/filtered axis; reification is a separate fact about the types.

findings.title: A `ResolvedGenerator` field description is ungrammatical and unparseable
locations: PAGE: api / Generator, `ResolvedGenerator` Fields: "the `û` whose displaced velocity `phase_shift.u_shifted` holds displaced velocity, left fresh by `velocity_rhs!`"
findings.description: PARAPHRASE fails outright — the relative clause has two heads and "displaced velocity" appears twice with no verb joining them. This is the only description of the field carrying the cross-verb freshness contract, so the one sentence a reader must understand is the one that cannot be read.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE, e.g. "the `û` the displaced velocity in `phase_shift.u_shifted` was recovered from".

findings.title: `deposit!` claims its argument order is shared with `step!` and then unlike `step!`
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `deposit!`: "The argument order is shared with `step!` — the cache leads because it is what this call mutates — unlike `step!`, whose leading `scheme` is a dispatch tag — and `state`, `domain`, `buffers` follow"
findings.description: One sentence, three em-dash interpolations, and an assertion followed by its own denial ("shared with" … "unlike"). The main clause and its completion ("and `state`, `domain`, `buffers` follow") sit 25 words apart, so the sentence loses its spine.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as two sentences: the leaders differ; the trailing three agree.

findings.title: The trajectory scheme is a live choice in the API and a single fixed scheme in the prose
locations: PAGE: api / Particles, `AbstractParticleIntegrator`: "Two members today: `EndpointHeun` … and `AdamsBashforth`"
PAGE: architecture, §4.6: "today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `advance!`: "Advects the tracers, if any, by Heun-in-time on the start- and end-of-step velocities"
PAGE: Home, Components: "`Particles`: Lagrangian tracer tracking — second-order advection"
findings.contradicts: The documented `AdamsBashforth` scheme and the `trajectory_scheme` keyword — axis: how many trajectory schemes exist.
findings.description: Three summary surfaces still describe tracking as unconditionally Heun. `advance!` is the worst instance: it states the scheme as fact where the constructor makes it a keyword, so a reader who passed `AdamsBashforth()` reads a docstring that denies their configuration.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE the three summaries to name the scheme axis, not one member.

findings.title: `ObservablesCache` documents an argument its signature does not show
locations: PAGE: api / Cache: "ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)"
PAGE: api / Cache, Arguments: "`history_depth = 1` — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over"
findings.contradicts: The displayed signature — axis: whether `history_depth` is a constructor keyword.
findings.description: The signature block is the first thing a reader copies. A documented keyword absent from it reads either as a stale signature or as an argument that does not exist, and the reader cannot tell which without trying it.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE the signature line to include `history_depth`.

findings.title: `recommended_cfl` refers to "the same scaling" before the scaling is introduced
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `recommended_cfl`: "The same $1/\kappa_{\max}$ scaling is applied to both schemes' bases, including `IFRK2`'s empirical one"
PAGE: api / Propagator, next paragraph: "It scales that base by the domain's dealiasing: … $C_{\mathrm{CFL}} \propto 1/\kappa_{\max}$."
findings.description: The paragraph qualifying the rule stands before the paragraph stating it, so "the same scaling" points forward at nothing, and "It" opens the later paragraph with no nearer antecedent than two paragraphs back. Read in order, the qualification is unreadable and the rule then arrives as repetition.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: state the scaling, then the caveat about IFRK2's base.

findings.title: `StationarityCriterion`: an 85-word sentence splits "measures ε … and k" by a 40-word aside
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `StationarityCriterion`: "At each iteration it measures the dissipation $\varepsilon$ — … which is why $k$ is kept out of the gate — and the kinetic energy $k$, which normalizes …"
findings.description: One sentence, ~85 words, five clauses (measures ε; why ε; why not k; measures k; tests flatness) plus a semicolon-joined sixth on stopping. The compound object of "measures" is broken across a 40-word interpolation that argues against measuring the second item, so "and the kinetic energy" arrives as a surprise.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as three sentences: what it samples; why ε and not k; what the flatness test does.

findings.title: `fields_modified!` promises that sanctioned mutators call it, then names one that does not
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, `fields_modified!`: "The sanctioned mutators call this for you: `step!` advances the epoch itself when it completes"
findings.contradicts: The claim's own evidence — axis: whether `step!` calls `fields_modified!`.
findings.description: The colon promises support for the claim and delivers a counter-example: `step!` advancing the epoch *itself* is precisely not a call to this function. A reader auditing a hand-run loop takes away the wrong invariant — that stepping announces an out-of-band mutation.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: "you do not need this after `step!`: it advances the epoch itself."

findings.title: Quick start: "drives k to that value" — "that value" has no antecedent
locations: PAGE: Home, Quick start: "# (the default forcing drives k to that value —"
PAGE: Home, Quick start, preceding comment: "# ν is set so the grid captures the dissipation scale"
findings.description: The deictic points at a value the visible code never shows: `kinetic_energy` is not passed, and the preceding comment is about ν. On the package's front page, the first sentence about forcing is unresolvable without leaving the page.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: name the default, e.g. "drives k to the default 1.5 (u′ = 1)".

findings.title: The docs deny a declaration API the reader is never shown — four times
locations: PAGE: observables_cache, §1.2: "Nothing is cached by request, and there is no vocabulary to declare"
PAGE: api / Cache, `ObservablesCache`: "The contents are automatic — derived from the configuration, never declared"
PAGE: api / Observables, `max_speed`: "rather than from anything a caller declares"
PAGE: observables_cache, §3.1 code comment: "# the slots follow the configuration — nothing is declared"
findings.description: UNPROVOKED DEFENCE. Nothing in the current surface offers a declaration keyword (it was removed), so each denial introduces the idea it refuses and sends the reader looking for a missing keyword. Once, in the design page, is a record; four times is a fossil field.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT three of the four; keep the design page's sentence.

findings.title: "An epoch is not an iteration number" is asserted in five places, the worked example twice
locations: PAGE: notation, Vocabulary: "Not an iteration number: an announced out-of-band mutation advances an epoch without advancing the clock."
PAGE: api / Cache, module: "An epoch counts changes to the state, not advances of the run"
PAGE: api / Cache, `ObservablesCache` Fields: "so it counts changes to the state rather than advances of the run"
PAGE: observables_cache, §1.3: "An epoch is therefore not an iteration number"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `current_step`: "after two steps and one announced mutation the clock reads step 2 and the fields epoch reads 4"
findings.description: DELETE test: any four can go with nothing lost, and the arithmetic example is repeated verbatim in the decision log and in `current_step`. The repetition signals the authors' anxiety about a past rename rather than any reader's need.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT: keep the glossary entry and the `current_step` example; let the rest link.

findings.title: "A `Simulation` is a container, not a reading surface" — a denial of forwarders no reader has met
locations: PAGE: Home, Components: "A `Simulation` is a container, not a reading surface"
PAGE: architecture, §4.7: "A `Simulation` is a container, not a reading surface (decision 49)"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, module: "the run layer adds no forwarding methods of its own"
findings.description: FOSSIL of the removed `velocity_physical(sim)` family. A reader arriving today has never seen a forwarded read; the sentence tells them one might exist and then denies it. The positive half — read the state through `sim.state`, the observables through `sim.cache` — carries all the information.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT the negative clause; keep the routing sentence.

findings.title: "nothing offers it as one" — the predictor velocity is refused four times over
locations: PAGE: architecture, §4.6: "never a sample of the flow, and nothing offers it as one"
PAGE: api / Particles, `ParticleIntegratorBuffers`: "so nothing in the package offers it as one"
PAGE: observables_cache, §2.5: "it belongs to no instant along the trajectory and is not exposed"
PAGE: observables_cache, §2.4 table: "velocity at the predicted particle position … never … the probe occupies no such position"
findings.description: UNPROVOKED DEFENCE, repeated. Each denial teaches the reader that a plausible-looking Lagrangian velocity sits within reach — the very reading the sentence exists to prevent. The field-level caution earns its place; the other three do not.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT to one, in the buffers docstring where the array is actually reachable.

findings.title: `ConstantPower`: "each stage" and "each step", "amplitude" and "rate", within two paragraphs
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, module map: "`ConstantPower` — a band amplitude re-solved each stage to hold the injection rate"
PAGE: api / Forcing, `ConstantPower`: "whose rate $A$ is set each step so the field's injection rate holds the `injection_rate`"
PAGE: api / Forcing, `ConstantPower`: "Since that amplitude is re-solved from the state, it enters the right-hand side at every stage"
findings.contradicts: The module map and architecture §4.4's "enter through the source at every stage" — axis: per-stage or per-step re-solve.
findings.description: "each step" is the odd one out, and it is the sentence that defines the strategy. The pronoun then swaps nouns: "that amplitude" refers back to a quantity introduced as the rate $A$, leaving the reader to decide whether one thing or two are being described.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: "each stage" throughout, and one noun for $A$.

findings.title: A section headed "What is not built" lists only what is built
locations: PAGE: observables_cache, §3.2 heading: "What is not built"
PAGE: observables_cache, §3.2 body: "The cache itself is built as §§1–2 describe … closes the list: the page and the code agree."
findings.contradicts: Its own heading — axis: whether the section records gaps.
findings.description: The heading promises a gap list and the body reports full coverage; "closes the list" refers to a list of absences that was never opened. A reader scanning headings for known limitations finds none and cannot tell whether the section is stale or the heading is wrong.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE the heading ("What is built, against §§1–2"), or state the remaining gap.

findings.title: Architecture run-on sentences: 110 words and five clauses in one breath
locations: PAGE: architecture, §4.1: "Its concrete type is the `FixedDomain`, the fixed, unsheared cube, realized by the grid, the real–Fourier layout, …" (≈110 words)
PAGE: architecture, §8: "The composite system factors as a tower … so the flow is a skew product and `advance!` is its Gauss–Seidel sweep in topological order" (≈90 words)
findings.description: Both sentences carry six or more listed items, each with its own aside, under a single main verb. Nothing in either is wrong; the shape fails — a reader cannot hold the enumeration open that long, and the §4.1 sentence buries its load-bearing "never materialized" claim mid-list.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE each as a lead sentence plus a bulleted list.

findings.title: The closing-deposit cost sentence carries four interpolations
locations: PAGE: observables_cache, §1.3: "so, relative to a cacheless solver …, the run pays one extra closing deposit — the state-only share of one first-stage evaluation, one reduction, and one interpolation — once per run"
findings.description: ~55 words, three clauses and two dash-pairs; "once per run" arrives 30 words after the verb it modifies. This states the cache's entire added cost — the one claim in §1.3 a sceptical reader will check — so it should be the shortest sentence in the section, not the longest.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as two sentences: the accounting, then what the extra deposit contains.

findings.title: "no per-point field is ever whole anywhere and none can be cached"
locations: PAGE: observables_cache, §1.2: "while no per-point field is ever whole anywhere and none can be cached"
findings.description: PARAPHRASE fails on "none": the plural has no plural antecedent (one field was named, in the negative), so the clause reads as a second claim about an unnamed set. "ever … anywhere" also doubles a quantifier the sentence already carries.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: "…while the speed field is never whole anywhere, so it cannot be cached."

findings.title: A parenthetical that concedes three names for one quantity
locations: PAGE: api / Particles, module map: "the same quantity the docs also call the Lagrangian velocity or the trajectory velocity"
findings.description: The clause reports the docs' own vocabulary drift instead of fixing it, and one synonym it promises ("trajectory velocity") appears nowhere else on the rendered site — a dead pointer offered as a reading aid.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT; the glossary already binds `particle_velocities` to its symbol.

findings.title: "It is a third bound, not the only one"
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation`, `max_dt`: "It is a third bound, not the only one: the adaptive step is the smallest of …"
findings.description: NON-VACUITY: "a third bound" already entails "not the only one"; the second clause restates the first, and the colon then supplies the actual content, so the whole opening is a run-up.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT to "The adaptive step is the smallest of …".

findings.title: Linear.indicator vs. band — one field named by implementation, three siblings named by meaning
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing — Linear Fields: '`indicator` — the band indicator as a real array.'
PAGE: api / Forcing — ConstantPower/VarianceController/VarianceRescaling Fields: '`band` — the band-pass kernel, lazy' / 'the band-pass kernel selecting the rescaled shells.'
findings.contradicts: Linear's field names the same conceptual object (the forced/rescaled band) that its three AbstractForcing siblings all call `band`.
findings.description: All four forcing strategies hold a per-mode band-selection object with the same meaning to the user: which shells are forced/rescaled. Three call it `band`; the one whose object happens to be materialized (not a lazy kernel) is instead called `indicator`, naming it for its backend representation rather than its meaning — violating rule (a).

findings.title: energy_spectrum (measured) and EnergySpectrum (predicted) share a name for non-interchangeable objects
locations: PAGE: api / Observables — 'What is returned is a per-shell energy E_n ... a model spectrum E(κ) from Phenomenology is instead a density per unit wavenumber ... not interchangeable.'
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra — 'EnergySpectrum <: TurbulenceLaw — Supertype of the velocity energy-spectrum models — parametrizations of E(κ).'
findings.description: Observables.energy_spectrum (a shell-summed E_n) and Phenomenology.Spectra.EnergySpectrum (a density E(κ)) carry the identical English name for two quantities the docs explicitly warn are not interchangeable — exactly the spectral-density-vs-energy category error the corpus's own doc policy guards against, here surfacing as a shared naming term across sibling modules.

findings.title: deposit_sample! and record_particle_velocities! carry crossed verbs
locations: PAGE: api / Cache — 'record_particle_velocities! writes, this call records.' (of deposit_sample!)
PAGE: notation (Vocabulary) — 'deposit | to write an observable into the cache and mark the moment it belongs to ... the tracer advance writes, deposit_sample! marks.'
findings.contradicts: The corpus's own Vocabulary defines 'deposit' as write+mark combined, yet deposit_sample! only marks while a function named with the verb 'record' does the writing — the verb in each function's name is not the verb used to describe its action.
findings.description: A reader who has internalized 'deposit = write and mark' will expect deposit_sample! to write the value; it does not. The two closely-paired functions' names do not track which of the two actions (write vs. mark) each performs.

findings.title: FlowConditions and Phenomenology.FlowParameters are near-identical names
locations: PAGE: api / Generator — 'Not to be confused with Phenomenology's FlowParameters, which shares two field names: this type holds what a run is configured with, that one holds what a run has been measured to have.'
findings.description: The docs carry an explicit disambiguation note for these two types — direct evidence the names are close enough to be mistaken for one another. Needing a 'not to be confused with' callout is the symptom of failing rule (b)'s one-reading test.

findings.title: u_consumed / ω_consumed name the argument for an implementation side effect, and inconsistently across siblings
locations: PAGE: api / Generator — 'velocity_rhs!(N̂, generator, û, u, ω_consumed, domain)'
PAGE: api / Generator — 'scalar_rhs!(N̂, generator, û, φ̂, u_consumed, φ, domain; ...)'
findings.contradicts: The same physical quantity (the physical velocity u) is named plain `u` in velocity_rhs!'s own signature and `u_consumed` in the sibling scalar_rhs! — one concept, two names, decided by which function happens to overwrite it.
findings.description: The `_consumed` suffix documents a backend aliasing side effect (the pointwise product overwrites the array) rather than what the argument physically is — naming for machinery/fate rather than meaning, a deliberate but rule-breaking choice per rule (a).

findings.title: IntegratorBuffers.stage1 denotes different objects per scheme
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator — '`stage1` — the first Runge–Kutta stage register, allocated by every scheme (the accumulator for IFLowStorageRK3, the first stage for IFRK2).'
findings.description: One storage-slot name means 'the low-storage accumulator h' under IFLowStorageRK3 and 'the literal first RK stage value' under IFRK2 — two different conceptual roles under one field name, violating rule (b)'s precision requirement for storage names.

findings.title: "Resolved" is documented as carrying two unrelated senses
locations: PAGE: notation (Vocabulary) — 'resolved | in ResolvedFields and ResolvedGenerator, made concrete as one value. The numerical sense — a scale the grid resolves ... — is the other reading, and the docs write it out in full wherever it is meant.'
findings.description: The corpus's own glossary admits 'resolved' is overloaded across the public surface (reification sense vs. numerical-resolution sense) and manages the collision only through prose, not through the type names themselves — ResolvedFields/ResolvedGenerator still carry the ambiguous word as load-bearing vocabulary.

findings.title: kinetic_energy names both a measuring function and a configured target
locations: PAGE: api / Observables — 'kinetic_energy(u) / kinetic_energy(û) — The turbulent kinetic energy ... of the velocity field.'
PAGE: api / SimulationRun — 'kinetic_energy = 1.5 — the initial, and when forced the held, kinetic energy k.'
findings.description: The exported Observables.kinetic_energy is a pure measurement of current state; Simulation's kinetic_energy keyword is a target/setpoint fed to the IC and the default controller. One identifier spans a diagnostic and a configuration input — the category conflation (measured value vs. configured target) the corpus's own doc policy warns against, here as a naming collision.

findings.title: Three names in circulation for one cached quantity
locations: PAGE: api / Particles — 'the trajectory velocities are read from the run's observables cache through particle_velocities — the same quantity the docs also call the Lagrangian velocity or the trajectory velocity.'
findings.description: The module docstring itself admits three names circulate for one quantity: the code identifier particle_velocities, plus the prose synonyms 'the Lagrangian velocity' and 'the trajectory velocity' — the code stays singular but the surrounding vocabulary does not, against rule (d).

findings.title: "Front door" is a software/business idiom promoted to formal glossary vocabulary
locations: PAGE: notation (Vocabulary) — 'front door | the Simulation constructor that builds every component from a few keywords, as against assembling the pieces yourself.'
findings.contradicts: CLAUDE.md's own naming register: 'the user is a physicist ... not a software engineer fluent in startup idiom.'
findings.description: 'Front door' is facade-pattern/product-design jargon, not a physics or numerics term, yet it is elevated to a repeatedly-used house term across the architecture doc and the notation page.

findings.title: Sreenivasan1998's fields break from the symbol-naming convention its siblings use
locations: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Scalings — 'Sreenivasan1998(; asymptote = 0.5, correction = 0.0)' vs. 'Sreenivasan1995(; C_K = 1.5)'
PAGE: api / phenomenology / StructureFunctions — 'Kolmogorov1941(; C₂ = 2.0)', 'Kolmogorov1962(; μ = 0.25)'
findings.description: Every other Phenomenology law preset names its fitted-constant field after its own published symbol (C_K, C₂, μ, β, α, c_L, c_η, p₀, C_OC); Sreenivasan1998 alone uses descriptive English (asymptote, correction) for the same role, possibly justified by symbol awkwardness but still the one exception to an otherwise uniform storage-naming convention.

findings.title: ObservablesCache's printed synopsis omits its real `history_depth` keyword
locations: api/Cache page: synopsis `ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)`, with `history_depth = 1` documented only in the # Arguments prose below it
src/Cache.jl: `function ObservablesCache(domain::FixedDomain; scalar::Bool = false, particle_velocities = nothing, history_depth::Integer = 1)`
findings.description: The checklist requires every signature argument documented 'from the signature'; here the failure is inverted — the docstring's own printed call form is missing a keyword its own Arguments bullet documents, so a reader who copies the shown synopsis never learns `history_depth` exists. Checked against every other constructor in the package (FixedDomain, Tracers, ConstantPower, Linear, VarianceController, VarianceRescaling, Simulation) — all keep the synopsis and real keyword set in lockstep or use an explicit `kwargs...` catch-all, which this one lacks. Looks isolated, not systemic.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `, history_depth = 1` to the synopsis line.

findings.title: Caveat admonition is not the docstring's last substantive block
locations: src/Observables.jl, derivative_skewness: after `!!! note "This is the run's largest transient allocation"`, a further un-admonitioned caveat about residual cubic-invariant aliasing, then a closing explanatory paragraph, both follow

src/Propagator.jl, recommended_cfl: after `!!! warning "The IFRK2 margin does not know the viscosity"`, two more substantive paragraphs follow (the shared 1/κ_max scaling, and the dealiasing-strategy scaling with a fresh Simulation cross-reference)
findings.description: CLAUDE.md's Template conventions state plainly: 'A caveat admonition is the last substantive block of a docstring, before # Fields — in a function docstring as in a type's.' In both instances real explanatory (and in recommended_cfl's case caveat-grade) content trails after the admonition instead of the admonition closing the docstring — exactly the shape the rule guards against, since a skimming reader stops at the admonition.
findings.resolution_hint: Fold the trailing caveats into (or ahead of) their admonitions so the admonition closes each docstring.

findings.title: VarianceController links VarianceRescaling twice in one docstring
locations: src/Forcing.jl, VarianceController docstring: 'Prefer it to [`VarianceRescaling`](@ref) whenever accuracy in time matters…' and later '…whose deterministic-rescaling limit is [`VarianceRescaling`](@ref).'
findings.description: CLAUDE.md: 'Link a target at most once per docstring — its first genuine mention.' A corpus-wide scan of every @ref link across all src/*.jl docstrings found exactly this one repeat; every other multiply-mentioned name in the package links once and falls back to a bare backtick afterward. VarianceController is the sole outlier.
findings.resolution_hint: Debacktick the second VarianceRescaling mention (drop its @ref).

findings.title: Load-bearing caveat left as plain prose instead of an admonition; Returns trails it
locations: src/Cache.jl, fields_modified!: 'It also discards the Lagrangian sample history this cache carries… would blend the old field into the new one.' then, only after, 'Returns `cache`.'
src/Cache.jl, particles_modified!: the same shape, ending 'Returns its argument.'
findings.description: CLAUDE.md's function-docstring order lists caveats 'as a !!! warning / !!! note where load-bearing' — silently discarding a multistep trajectory scheme's sample history is exactly load-bearing (compare ObservablesCache's own sibling caveat on cache-array reuse, which IS an admonition here). Separately, the Doc-edit checklist places 'Returns x.' before any caveat admonition; here Returns is the final line, after the (un-admonitioned) caveat.
findings.resolution_hint: Promote the discard-of-history sentence to !!! warning and move the Returns sentence ahead of it.

findings.title: §4.6 / CLAUDE.md still describe the trajectory-scheme axis as un-built, though decision 57 built AdamsBashforth
locations: ARCHITECTURE.md §4.6: "the trajectory scheme — today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
CLAUDE.md Particles bullet: "the pluggable trajectory integrator (`AbstractParticleIntegrator`, `EndpointHeun`)" (no AdamsBashforth)
ARCHITECTURE.md decision 33: "The particle-scheme axis has one point today (the Heun scheme)"
findings.contradicts: ARCHITECTURE.md decision 57 ("A second trajectory scheme: variable-step Adams–Bashforth") and the rendered api/Particles page ("Two members today: `EndpointHeun`... and `AdamsBashforth`"); confirmed live and exported in src/Particles.jl (AdamsBashforth type, MultistepBuffers, allocate_buffers, advect!, restart!, history_depth all implemented).
findings.description: Three current-state surfaces (architecture §4.6, CLAUDE.md's module map, and decision 33's audit-coverage description) state or imply EndpointHeun is the only trajectory scheme and a second scheme is still future work. Decision 57, in the same document, built and shipped exactly that second scheme (AdamsBashforth), live in the API and source. Unlike decisions 15/20/26, no "(Superseded by decision N...)" annotation was added to reconcile the older text.
findings.resolution_hint: Update §4.6 and CLAUDE.md's Particles bullet to name both schemes; amend or annotate decision 33's particle-scheme-axis claim.

findings.title: Decision 46 states the include order backwards vs. §4.9, CLAUDE.md, and the actual source
locations: ARCHITECTURE.md decision 46: "The include order becomes `State → Observables → Cache`"
findings.contradicts: ARCHITECTURE.md §4.9 Layout summary ("SimulationDomain → Observables → State → Cache → ..."); CLAUDE.md's "Include order: SimulationDomain → Observables → State → Cache → ..."; src/GBGIsotropicTurbulence.jl's actual include() sequence (Observables included before State) and its own header comment explaining why Observables must precede State (seeders call Observables' reductions to rescale to a target energy/variance).
findings.description: Decision 46's headline ("Observables precedes Cache") is correct, but the arrow inside the entry has State before Observables — the reverse of every other current-state surface and the shipped code. This is a directional error in the entry describing the very reorganization whose result is Observables-before-State everywhere else, not a case of exempt historical vocabulary.
findings.resolution_hint: Fix decision 46's arrow to Observables → State → Cache.

findings.title: Decision 35's readback count was rewritten to the current default with only the parenthetical preserving the original finding
locations: ARCHITECTURE.md decision 35: "the default configuration issues ten blocking readbacks per step ... plus VarianceController's three reductions" followed by "(Three when this was written, under the VarianceRescaling default; decision 58 changed the default, and the count with it...)"
findings.contradicts: The entry's own parenthetical, which states the true count when the decision was written was three (under VarianceRescaling) — the reverse of the pattern used elsewhere (decisions 15/20/26), where the original claim stays in the main clause and the parenthetical supplies the later correction.
findings.description: The main clause of decision 35 has been silently rewritten to describe the present (post-decision-58) configuration, while its own parenthetical admits the number was different "when this was written." A reader can no longer tell from the body alone what was actually measured in 2026-07.
findings.resolution_hint: Either restore the as-written number/forcing to the main clause and let the parenthetical state the current number, or explicitly date the main clause's claim to decision 58.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md §4.6 still claims EndpointHeun is "the single" trajectory scheme, orphaned by decision 57's AdamsBashforth
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4.6 (Particles): "the trajectory scheme — today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
Same file, decision log entry 57 (commit 3cd3ec7, 2026-08-19): "A second trajectory scheme: variable-step Adams–Bashforth."
Rendered api/Particles page, AbstractParticleIntegrator docstring: "Two members today: `EndpointHeun`... and `AdamsBashforth`..."
findings.contradicts: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §7 decision 57 and the Particles API page both say AdamsBashforth is a second, already-built trajectory scheme; §4.6's narrative prose says only one exists and calls a second one a future axis — same document, three sections apart.
findings.description: Commit 3cd3ec7 added AdamsBashforth, wrote decision 57, and updated Particles.jl's own docstrings/API page, but never touched the §4.6 architectural narrative paragraph describing the particle numerics, which predates decision 50 (when EndpointHeun really was the only scheme). The sentence is now a live 'today' claim falsified by the same file's own decision log and by the AdamsBashforth docstring three pages later in the rendered site.

findings.title: ObservablesCache's quick-reference signature omits history_depth, which its own Arguments list documents
locations: src/Cache.jl (rendered api/Cache), top synopsis: "ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)"
Same docstring, # Arguments, four lines later: "history_depth = 1 — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over..."
docs/docstring_shape.csv and docs/make.jl baseline key: literally "Cache.jl::ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)" — copied from the same incomplete synopsis
findings.contradicts: The docstring's own printed call signature (top) omits a keyword that the same docstring's own Arguments section (four lines down) documents in full, and that the actual `function ObservablesCache(...; history_depth::Integer = 1)` requires.
findings.description: history_depth was introduced by commit 177d5b6 (2026-08-20, 'Move the Lagrangian sample history into the ObservablesCache; close the AB-reseed defect') to support AdamsBashforth's velocity-history need. That commit widened the constructor and its # Arguments section but never updated the one-line call synopsis at the docstring's own top, which a skimming reader treats as the whole signature. The stale string is even hard-coded into the docstring-shape lint baseline, generated from the same incomplete synopsis, so the lint cannot catch the drift.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's Particles line still names only EndpointHeun as the trajectory scheme (twin-copy of finding 1)
locations: CLAUDE.md, Modules and wiring: "the pluggable trajectory integrator (`AbstractParticleIntegrator`, `EndpointHeun`)"
Contradicted by decision 57 (AdamsBashforth) and by the Particles API page enumerating both schemes
findings.contradicts: Same axis as finding 1: CLAUDE.md names exactly one concrete of AbstractParticleIntegrator where a second (AdamsBashforth) has existed since 2026-08-19.
findings.description: Lower confidence than finding 1 because CLAUDE.md is deliberately terse and mostly omits concretes elsewhere (Propagator names only AbstractIntegrator, not IFLowStorageRK3/IFRK2), so this could read as 'one example' rather than a completeness claim. But it cites decision 50, which predates decision 57 and was never revisited, and is the twin-copy sibling of finding 1's fossil.

findings.title: Admonition-title rule: PF unconditional, IT conditional
locations: IT CLAUDE.md Template conventions: 'stays a bare `!!! note` when it is a general aside'
PF CLAUDE.md docstring rubric (3): 'Every `!!!` block carries a custom descriptive title... never a bare `!!! warning`'
findings.description: PF's rule bans bare admonitions unconditionally; IT's explicitly permits them for general asides. A real split in an otherwise near-verbatim shared rule, with no decision recorded for the loosening.
findings.contradicts: PF: 'every ... never a bare' vs IT: 'stays a bare !!! note when it is a general aside'

findings.title: PF has a consent gate for expensive verification lanes; IT has none
locations: PF CLAUDE.md: 'Consent gate (user-directed 2026-08-04) — unasked, run ONLY Pkg.test()'
IT CLAUDE.md 'Verification workflow' section (no gating language)
findings.description: PF requires explicit user consent before any expensive lane (exhaustive survey, benchmarks, GPU suites, /check-docs, /check-consistency). IT bundles three audits into its default Pkg.test() gate and has its own expensive multi-agent lanes (/check-docs, /check-consistency) with no equivalent consent language anywhere in CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: IT's type-docstring template is richer (constructor-first, Examples policy) than PF's minimal fields-only rule
locations: PF CLAUDE.md: 'A type... documents them under `The fields are`... prose is reserved for the one-sentence identity above that list' (the only type rule stated)
IT CLAUDE.md: 'Type docstring = home, constructor-first... (3) an example where the construction is non-obvious...'
findings.description: PF's rulebook never codifies a constructor-first order, an Examples-section policy, or a positional-constructor-naming rule, though PF's own Grid3D docstring practice already gestures toward it. Good candidate to port IT's richer template back into PF.

findings.title: Citation link form: PF one titled form everywhere; IT two different forms by surface
locations: PF CLAUDE.md: 'Every reference carries a clickable DOI on its title — [*Title*](https://doi.org/…)... verbatim-identical in the §References list and every inline docstring copy'
IT CLAUDE.md: '§References entry ends in a bare autolink... inline docstring cite uses the labelled [doi:10.…](https://doi.org/…)'
findings.description: PF's inline citation always keeps the paper title; IT's inline form drops it in favour of a bare DOI label, verified only by decoded-identifier match rather than literal identity. Adjudicated as fine within IT; named here as a genuine cross-package architecture split.

findings.title: PF codifies an author-count truncation rule for citations; IT's rulebook never states one
locations: PF CLAUDE.md: 'Name up to three authors... four or more → First et al.'
IT CLAUDE.md documentation-policy paragraph (no author-count rule stated anywhere)
findings.description: IT's practice matches PF's unwritten convention (et al. in-text, full names in the bibliography even at 8-9 authors), but the rule itself is absent from IT's CLAUDE.md — a documentation-completeness gap.

findings.title: Citation placement: PF places it last in the docstring template, IT lets it open the identity sentence
locations: PF CLAUDE.md: citation is order-item (6) of 7, after the formula, before cross-links
IT CLAUDE.md: 'may open the identity sentence when the citation names the method ("the smooth spectral filter of Hou & Li (2007) …")'
findings.description: A real template-order divergence, plausibly a deliberate physics-prose adaptation rather than a defect; already adjudicated as fine within IT alone.

findings.title: IT bans \mathbf outright (build-enforced); PF has no such ban and uses it deliberately
locations: IT CLAUDE.md: 'never upright \mathbf (build-enforced)'
PF CLAUDE.md: 'for the indicator/identity write \mathbf{1}...' and 'the example's bold \mathbf{k} stays'
findings.description: Likely a sound adaptation (IT's vectors are uniformly boldsymbol, no indicator-matrix apparatus), but a genuine, not merely apparent, notation-rule divergence between the two rulebooks.

findings.title: IT's TeX-idiom block credits PF wholesale but adds a \mid rule PF's own list lacks
locations: IT CLAUDE.md: '(adopted from PF 2026-08-06...); a conditional bar is \mid'
PF CLAUDE.md 'Math spacing and command support' section — no rule about \mid anywhere
findings.description: The attribution covers the block as a whole but at least one clause (\mid) is not present in PF's stated rules — a mild overstatement of provenance, and a candidate for PF to adopt for symmetry.

findings.title: IT built a docstring-growth/shape lint; PF's build lints lack an equivalent despite the same bloat history
locations: IT CLAUDE.md: 'lint_docstring_shape() fails on a docstring that grew since docstring_shape.csv was last written'
PF CLAUDE.md names only lint_inline_math(), lint_notation_variants(), lint_retired_claims()
findings.description: A genuine tooling asymmetry; PF's own file documents the identical multi-round-patch bloat failure mode in prose without a build guard for it — a plausible forward-transfer candidate.

findings.title: PF has a documented examples/ pipeline and a 'run the examples' definition-of-done item; IT has neither
locations: PF CLAUDE.md: extensive examples/ Literate-doc-page rules + 'Definition of done' item 6 'The examples, RUN'
IT: no examples/ directory exists; CLAUDE.md never mentions one
findings.description: Not a documentation defect — IT hasn't built worked examples yet — but a scope gap worth naming, since PF's own history shows exactly this gap shipping silent breakages.

locations: IT CLAUDE.md: four-item 'Known weaknesses — self-guards' section
PF CLAUDE.md: no equivalent section anywhere
findings.description: Likely reflects IT-specific session history rather than a PF gap; named per the brief's instruction to note asymmetric rules even when one-sided.

findings.title: IT's 'Template conventions' is a consolidated checkable-rules list; PF's equivalent material is scattered and missing two discriminators
locations: IT CLAUDE.md: 'Template conventions, stated so the split is checkable' — eight bullets including Returns x. and -> Type arrow rules
